style_when: the news is structural and abstract — a stack reordered, a layer added, a flow rerouted — and there is no literal object that carries it, so the idea is stated as a small physical assembly of recognisable parts rather than as bare shapes
prompt: Matte clay 3D render of a modular server memory assembly resting on a weathered concrete surface in a real space. The physical arrangement features three recognizable engineered parts: a slotted data housing block, a heavy open mechanical latch acting as a security gate, and a single distinct memory cartridge positioned just outside the write slot. Matte surfaces with subtle moulding seams and realistic contact shadows. One directional key light raking across the concrete from the left, casting long shadows. Muted modern editorial palette with a terracotta accent on the incoming cartridge. Wide landscape composition, heavy asymmetric layout with the assembly anchored in the lower right, generous empty margin.
negative_prompt: text, watermarks, logos, UI, typography, legible print, letters, numbers
rationale: Clay render is ideal for structural software concepts like memory storage layers, translating a digital write path into a tangible, modular physical assembly of drives and gates.
cue: the control belongs at the store boundary
subject: modular memory drive assembly with a security latch
